business_problem: Xiangji Technology needed a cost-effective way to process and serve massive weather-observation, numerical-model, and satellite datasets. Accurate commercial weather forecasting depends on heavy computation and constant product iteration, but building enough on-premises infrastructure for that workload was too expensive for a growing specialist company.
solution_summary: Xiangji Technology built its commercial weather-intelligence stack on Alibaba Cloud so it could turn large-scale meteorological data into industry services without carrying the cost of self-managed infrastructure. The company's Gavial spatiotemporal data platform acts as a PaaS layer for large weather datasets, handling large-volume query, processing, scheduling, and development needs. On top of that, the AI-Weather forecasting core combines machine learning with numerical weather models so the company can cover basic meteorological elements, more complex weather features, and domain-specific forecast adjustments for customers in agriculture, logistics, transport, retail, and energy. Xiangji has used Alibaba Cloud since 2015, relying on elastic compute and cloud-native container capabilities to reduce R&D cost while keeping customer data safe. The result is a commercial weather platform where AI improves forecast post-processing and industry delivery instead of remaining a research-only tool.

solution_components.name: Gavial Spatiotemporal Data Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the PaaS framework for weather-data query, processing, scheduling, and application plugins.

solution_components.name: AI-Weather
solution_components.role: Combines machine learning and numerical models to generate commercial weather forecasts.

solution_components.name: Elastic Compute Service (ECS)
solution_components.role: Supplies elastic compute for meteorological model and application workloads.

solution_components.name: Cloud-native containers
solution_components.role: Support cloud-native packaging and deployment of forecasting services.

data_flow: Observation feeds, numerical model outputs, and satellite remote-sensing data are ingested into Gavial, where they are processed and combined with Xiangji's AI-Weather engine. The forecast outputs are then delivered to downstream industry customers as decision-support services for operations, risk reduction, and planning.
business_outcome: Xiangji used Alibaba Cloud to industrialize commercial forecasting without overbuilding local infrastructure. The platform lowered development cost, improved deployment flexibility, and gave the company a scalable path to serve more weather-sensitive industries with data-rich AI forecasting products.
architecture_clues: The forecasting stack separates a data PaaS layer from the predictive AI core rather than collapsing everything into one model service.
AI is applied mainly to post-process and improve prediction quality on top of numerical weather modeling.
The business depends on multi-source meteorological data, including observation, model, and satellite streams.
